source.author: verg
source.text: Huic deus ipse loci fluvio Tiberinus amoeno populeas inter senior se attollere frondes visus; eum tenuis glauco velabat amictu carbasus, et crinis umbrosa tegebat harundo, tum sic affari et curas his demere dictis:
source.text_original: Huic deus ipse loci fluvio Tiberinus amoeno / populeas inter senior se attollere frondes / visus; eum tenuis glauco velabat amictu / carbasus, et crinis umbrosa tegebat harundo, / tum sic affari et curas his demere dictis: /
source.text_english: To him the god of the place himself, Tiberinus, seemed to rise from amid the pleasant poplar leaves by the river; a fine linen garment in bluish green covered him, and a shady reed covered his hair. Then he spoke thus and took away his cares with these words:

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: subita cur pulcher harundine crines velat Hylas?
reuse.text_original: subita cur pulcher harundine crines / velat Hylas?
reuse.text_english: Why does beautiful Hylas suddenly veil his hair with a reed?
